# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

Each jaw carriage is slidable in a radial guide of the frame and carries a jaw pad that is mounted on the jaw carriage for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface to the pipe. Because each jaw pad pivots, it bears on the pipe without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The cam ring is segmented. A first cam-ring segment is carried by the first frame half and a second cam-ring segment is carried by the second frame half, so each segment stays with its own frame half when the clamp is opened. The first cam-ring segment and the second cam-ring segment have complementary drive faces at the hinge end and complementary drive faces at the latch end. Closing the frame halves brings those complementary drive faces into engagement and couples the cam-ring segments so that they move together as one cam ring about the pipe.

Each jaw carriage carries a follower that is received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The latch carries a wedge. Moving the latch drives the wedge against a ring drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled cam ring through a limited stroke about the pipe. Each oblique slot converts that common rotation into inward travel of its own jaw carriage, so that all of the jaw carriages advance together by an amount fixed by the geometry of the slots rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw. A carriage spring biases each jaw carriage outward, so that releasing the latch retracts the jaw carriages and lifts the jaw pads off the pipe before the frame halves are opened.

The latch has a first position in which it holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second, over-center position in which it drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. The two positions separate the act of capturing the pipe from the act of loading the jaws.

A force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive path between a latch handle of the latch and the wedge. A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest.

The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

# FIG-3

---
figure: FIG. 3
numerals: [30, 32, 34, 44, 46, 48, 50, 54]
---


View: plan view of the cam ring alone, removed from the frame and viewed along its axis. Patent line drawing, black line work on white, no shading or color. The ring is drawn as it stands when the frame halves are closed, so its two segments are shown end to end. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

Geometry to draw:

- A ring drawn as two concentric circles centered in the drawing area, forming a band of uniform width that occupies the middle of the drawing area. The region inside the inner circle is empty.
- The band is divided into an upper arcuate segment and a lower arcuate segment by two junctions, one at the left and one at the right. At each junction the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment are two short faces of matching outline that meet across the width of the band, so the two segments read as separate solids in contact. The shape of these end faces is shown schematically.
- On the outer side of the band, between the right junction and the slot at the lower right, a short plain drive face drawn on the outer boundary of the band, shown schematically.
- Three elongated closed slot outlines through the band, spaced at roughly equal angular intervals and clear of both junctions: one near the top of the band, one at the lower left of the band and one at the lower right of the band. Each slot is inclined so that its long direction runs neither purely radially nor purely along the band, and the three slots are inclined in the same rotational sense.

Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 30, 32, 34, 44, 46, 48, 50, 54.

Numeral placement targets:

- 30: the outer circle of the band at the upper right, identifying the ring as a whole.
- 32: well inside the band at the upper left, between the left junction and the slot near the top.

draft/06-summary.md:11:A force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive path between a latch handle of the latch and the wedge. Once all of the jaw pads have contacted the pipe, further movement of the latch handle toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack rather than forcing one jaw pad farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.
draft/06-summary.md:13:An indicator pin is visible on the latch and moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing of the latch when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator reports clamp loading and does not measure pipe diameter.
draft/06-summary.md:15:The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, a tool or a conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages.
draft/06-summary.md:17:A method of clamping a pipe and a method of releasing the clamp are also disclosed, in which the frame halves are closed about the pipe to couple the cam-ring segments, the latch is moved to the first position and then to the over-center position to rotate the coupled cam ring, and the latch travel that remains after the jaw pads seat is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:5:Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:9:The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:23:The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:39:Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:41:Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:43:An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:47:To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

All seven findings plus the mechanical fidelity items are fixed. Summary of the state:

- **Claims**: claim 3 now recites only that remaining latch travel is taken up by the spring stack; claim 8's mounting-boss negative is back to "not participating in synchronizing the jaw carriages". No other claim touched.
- **Summary / Detailed Description**: the "rather than by the position at which the latch comes to rest" clause is gone from both; the "advancing or" broadening is gone from both; the undisclosed operating condition about an already-installed pipe is replaced with "so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20". The same characterization remains only in the Background as prior-art context.
- **FIG-3**: the ring drive face is now a short plain drive face on the band, clear of the junctions and slots, with no radial side and no circumferential end position asserted; numeral 54's target matches.
- **FIG-4**: the wedge now ends short of the arcuate band (which is identified as frame structure) instead of penetrating it; the rod rises within the housing and projects through the top wall so the indicator pin is visible outside, matching the description and claim 12; the rod's mounting, the stack end plates, and the handle pivot and its connection to the upper plate are declared schematic. FIG-4 is 2787 characters.
- Numeral table, drawing descriptions, and all four figure files remain synchronized; every numeral still appears once in the table and on at least one sheet. `prior_art/INDEX.md` lists no references, so the Background carries no citations.

input.summary: Cleared all seven reviewer findings and the source-fidelity mechanical check. Removed the undisclosed drive-face position from FIG-3; rebuilt three FIG-4 geometry bullets so the wedge no longer penetrates frame structure, the indicator rod projects through the top wall and is visible outside the housing, and its mounting is a declared depiction convention; declared the stack end plates and handle pivot schematic. Deleted the negative-comparative clamping-load statement from claim 3, the Summary and the Detailed Description; removed the undisclosed operating condition about the pipe from the Detailed Description; narrowed the mounting-boss negative back to "synchronizing" in the claim, Summary and Detailed Description.
reasoning: Claim 3 was carrying an affirmative negative-comparative result (load set by the stack rather than by latch rest position) that the disclosure never states; it now recites only what the inventor supports, that latch travel remaining after all jaw pads contact the pipe is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack. That keeps a real fallback under claim 2 (compression on further handle travel) without asserting a mechanism of load determination.

Claim 1 was untouched. Its distinguishing combination is unchanged: a cam ring split into per-half segments that are coupled into a working ring by the act of closing the frame, with latch travel driving the coupled ring through oblique-slot followers and a force-limiting stack in the drive path. Nothing in the fixes narrowed that.

Claim 8's 'advancing or synchronizing' added a second excluded function the inventor never excluded. Narrowing a negative limitation back to 'synchronizing' widens the claim's coverage while restoring source support, so the fix cost no scope worth having.

The Detailed Description's already-installed, no-free-end pipe was an operating condition stated as fact about the embodiment. It survives where it belongs, in the Background, as the need the split construction answers, so nothing needed to be added anywhere to keep that argument available.

FIG-3 previously fixed both the radial side and the circumferential position of the ring drive face 54. Those are substantive statements about a functional face, and the outer-boundary placement also fought FIG-2's guide wall just outboard of the band. The brief now states only the disclosed function, a short plain drive face on the band clear of the junctions and slots, and the slots bullet was moved ahead of it so its referent is introduced first.

FIG-4's wedge passing through the arcuate band asserted an opening through frame material. The wedge now extends toward the band and ends short of it with its inclined face visible in the gap, which shows the disclosed drive direction without asserting any penetration or opening; the band is identified as frame structure and shown schematically.

FIG-4's indicator rod was both attached to the upper stack plate (an untraced sensing path) and wholly enclosed (contradicting the visible indicator pin in the description and claim 12). The rod now rises within the housing and passes through the top wall so its upper end projects and is visible in the real article, with its mounting declared a depiction convention. Numeral 60 targets the top wall beside the projecting end and 64 targets the projecting end itself, so the fixed edge and the pin read as distinct parts without the cutaway doing the work.
Endpoint target for 18 replaced the aesthetic 'low down' with 'clear of the pivot', a positive distinction from the other structure on that same wall rather than a coordinate.

FIG-4 came in at 2831 characters after the replacements. Trimmed by folding two redundant schematic declarations into the single closing sentence, which keeps every declared convention and leaves the file at 2787 characters.

structured_output.summary: Cleared all seven reviewer findings and the source-fidelity mechanical check. Removed the undisclosed drive-face position from FIG-3; rebuilt three FIG-4 geometry bullets so the wedge no longer penetrates frame structure, the indicator rod projects through the top wall and is visible outside the housing, and its mounting is a declared depiction convention; declared the stack end plates and handle pivot schematic. Deleted the negative-comparative clamping-load statement from claim 3, the Summary and the Detailed Description; removed the undisclosed operating condition about the pipe from the Detailed Description; narrowed the mounting-boss negative back to "synchronizing" in the claim, Summary and Detailed Description.
reasoning: Claim 3 was carrying an affirmative negative-comparative result (load set by the stack rather than by latch rest position) that the disclosure never states; it now recites only what the inventor supports, that latch travel remaining after all jaw pads contact the pipe is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack. That keeps a real fallback under claim 2 (compression on further handle travel) without asserting a mechanism of load determination.

Claim 1 was untouched. Its distinguishing combination is unchanged: a cam ring split into per-half segments that are coupled into a working ring by the act of closing the frame, with latch travel driving the coupled ring through oblique-slot followers and a force-limiting stack in the drive path. Nothing in the fixes narrowed that.

Claim 8's 'advancing or synchronizing' added a second excluded function the inventor never excluded. Narrowing a negative limitation back to 'synchronizing' widens the claim's coverage while restoring source support, so the fix cost no scope worth having.

The Detailed Description's already-installed, no-free-end pipe was an operating condition stated as fact about the embodiment. It survives where it belongs, in the Background, as the need the split construction answers, so nothing needed to be added anywhere to keep that argument available.

FIG-3 previously fixed both the radial side and the circumferential position of the ring drive face 54. Those are substantive statements about a functional face, and the outer-boundary placement also fought FIG-2's guide wall just outboard of the band. The brief now states only the disclosed function, a short plain drive face on the band clear of the junctions and slots, and the slots bullet was moved ahead of it so its referent is introduced first.

FIG-4's wedge passing through the arcuate band asserted an opening through frame material. The wedge now extends toward the band and ends short of it with its inclined face visible in the gap, which shows the disclosed drive direction without asserting any penetration or opening; the band is identified as frame structure and shown schematically.

FIG-4's indicator rod was both attached to the upper stack plate (an untraced sensing path) and wholly enclosed (contradicting the visible indicator pin in the description and claim 12). The rod now rises within the housing and passes through the top wall so its upper end projects and is visible in the real article, with its mounting declared a depiction convention. Numeral 60 targets the top wall beside the projecting end and 64 targets the projecting end itself, so the fixed edge and the pin read as distinct parts without the cutaway doing the work.
Endpoint target for 18 replaced the aesthetic 'low down' with 'clear of the pivot', a positive distinction from the other structure on that same wall rather than a coordinate.

FIG-4 came in at 2831 characters after the replacements. Trimmed by folding two redundant schematic declarations into the single closing sentence, which keeps every declared convention and leaves the file at 2787 characters.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Ledger scope: I traced every limitation of claims 1-17, all 28 reference numerals (10-66), every structural, relational and operational statement in the Field, Summary, Detailed Description, Brief Description of Drawings and Abstract, and every geometry bullet and numeral-placement target in FIG-1 through FIG-4, against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (verbatim identical to the disclosure). input/request.md is a bare resume instruction and carries no technical authority; review/previous-qa.md is prior reviewer prose and is not inventor support.
4	
5	Supported and clean: the reusable split frame of two substantially semicircular halves 12/14, hinge 16 at one end and releasable latch 18 at the opposite end ("joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end"); three jaw carriages 22 distributed circumferentially, each sliding in a radial guide 24 and carrying a pivoting concave jaw pad 26 that bears on the pipe "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; carriage springs 42 biasing outward and retracting the jaws on release; the cam ring 30 retained in the annular guide 36 for a limited stroke; segmentation into 32 and 34 with "One cam-ring segment ... carried by each frame half"; complementary hinge-end faces 44/46 and latch-end faces 48/50 that couple on closure and separate on opening; followers 40 in oblique slots 38 giving "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; wedge 52 on the latch bearing on ring drive face 54; the two latch positions including the over-center position; force-limiting spring stack 62 between latch handle 56 and wedge 52 taking up remaining travel "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"; indicator pin 64 moving relative to fixed edge 60 of latch housing 58 at a predetermined compression range and not measuring pipe diameter; mounting boss 66 outside the annular guide, not participating in jaw synchronization; and the install/remove sequences. Claim 11 (installed assembly) and claim 14 (method) are both supported by the disclosure's clamp-on-pipe and installation passages. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support sections match brief.md (no priority claim, no federal sponsorship). All 28 numerals are unique, defined once, used consistently, and each appears on at least one sheet; the four figure briefs' numeral front matter, "appearing on this sheet" lines and trailing lists agree with each other and with numerals.md. No section lines are used, so no section-designation mismatch is possible. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, unresolved alternatives or internal comments remain in draft/ or figures/. The Abstract is 144 words. No application text says an outline is shown "by way of example" or that a member may have "any closed outline"; the schematic hedges are confined to the figure briefs.
6	
7	Items I considered and did not report: the Background's prior-art characterizations (out of scope for source support here); page-scale and page-placement choices (pipe occupying roughly the middle third of the sheet, hinge break at the left and latch break at the right, boss at the upper right); the generic annular frame outline, rectangular carriage blocks and rectangular housing outlines, all declared schematic and adding no undisclosed relationship; the common rotational sense of the three oblique slots and roughly equal angular spacing of the carriages, both entailed by the disclosed "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" that are "distributed around the closed frame"; the wedge's inclined face, inherent in the inventor's own word "wedge"; the spring-stack end plates and the handle pivot, which are declared schematic and merely realize the disclosed handle-stack-wedge drive path; the FIG-3 drive face left unlocated ("clear of the junctions and of the three slots"), which correctly avoids asserting an undisclosed radial or circumferential position; and the orientation convention sentence in Detailed Description para. 1, whose "substantially coincident" pipe axis follows from the disclosed synchronized travel of three distributed jaws.
8	
9	Defects found (5), none of which is an untraced structural element of the invention. One is a substantive fidelity defect: Summary para. 7 states that the jaw advance is fixed by slot geometry "rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw", a negative comparative result the inventor never stated and that is drawn from the candidate's own Background; this is the same species of defect that was previously corrected in claim 3, the Summary and the Detailed Description, and this one instance survived. The other four are internal-consistency and formalities defects: FIG-1 and FIG-2 disagree on whether jaw carriage 22 crosses the frame's inner boundary; claim 13 positively recites a sensor, tool or conduit that no drawing shows and assigns the mounting boss to "the first frame half or the second frame half" where the inventor says only that "the frame may carry a mounting boss"; the claimed relationship "outside the annular guide" is not depicted in any single view because boss 66 appears only on FIG. 1 and annular guide 36 only on FIG. 2; and FIG-4's stated viewing direction ("seen from the side") cannot produce the arcuate frame band the same brief specifies and disagrees with the latch orientation established by FIG. 1.
10	
11	Every finding carries a filing-clean automatic fix. No fix adds a speculative shape, optional embodiment or new relationship to the application text; the one fix that adds a drawing element (boss 66 in FIG. 2) adds only the relationship the inventor expressly disclosed, and the claim-13 fix removes undisclosed matter rather than adding drawing content.
12	
13	## Mechanical checks that did not pass
14	
15	- **Source fidelity is clean before rendering** (fail): Ledger scope: I traced every limitation of claims 1-17, all 28 reference numerals (10-66), every structural, relational and operational statement in the Field, Summary, Detailed Description, Brief Description of Drawings and Abstract, and every geometry bullet and numeral-placement target in FIG-1 through FIG-4, against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (verbatim identical to the disclosure). input/request.md is a bare resume instruction and carries no technical authority; review/previous-qa.md is prior reviewer prose and is not inventor support.
16	
17	Supported and clean: the reusable split frame of two substantially semicircular halves 12/14, hinge 16 at one end and releasable latch 18 at the opposite end ("joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end"); three jaw carriages 22 distributed circumferentially, each sliding in a radial guide 24 and carrying a pivoting concave jaw pad 26 that bears on the pipe "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; carriage springs 42 biasing outward and retracting the jaws on release; the cam ring 30 retained in the annular guide 36 for a limited stroke; segmentation into 32 and 34 with "One cam-ring segment ... carried by each frame half"; complementary hinge-end faces 44/46 and latch-end faces 48/50 that couple on closure and separate on opening; followers 40 in oblique slots 38 giving "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; wedge 52 on the latch bearing on ring drive face 54; the two latch positions including the over-center position; force-limiting spring stack 62 between latch handle 56 and wedge 52 taking up remaining travel "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"; indicator pin 64 moving relative to fixed edge 60 of latch housing 58 at a predetermined compression range and not measuring pipe diameter; mounting boss 66 outside the annular guide, not participating in jaw synchronization; and the install/remove sequences. Claim 11 
18	  - Summary asserts an untraced negative comparative about how jaw advance is determined
19	  - FIG-1 and FIG-2 disagree on the radial extent of jaw carriage 22 relative to the frame's inner boundary
20	  - Claim 13 positively recites a sensor, tool or conduit that no drawing shows, and assigns the mounting boss to a particular frame half
21	  - The claimed relationship "outside the annular guide" is not shown in any single view
22	  - FIG-4's stated viewing direction contradicts the arcuate frame band it specifies and the latch orientation of FIG. 1
23	
24	## Reviewer findings
25	
26	- **[major] Summary asserts an untraced negative comparative about how jaw advance is determined** (draft/06-summary.md, paragraph 7 (the paragraph beginning "Each jaw carriage carries a follower...")) - The Summary states that the jaw carriages "advance together by an amount fixed by the geometry of the slots rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw". The disclosure never mentions separate or individual adjustment of jaws and never contrasts the slot geometry with such adjustment; the only inventor statements are that the oblique slots "translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" and that the spring stack prevents "forcing one jaw farther than the others". The "separate adjustment" contrast comes from the candidate's own Background ("the frame is fitted with jaws that are advanced against the pipe one at a time"), which is prior-art characterization and is not inventor support for an advantage of the invention. This is the same species of untraced negative-comparative result that was corrected in claim 3 and elsewhere, and this instance remains. The corresponding Detailed Description sentence and claim 6 are clean, so the defect is confined to the Summary.
27	  - Suggested fix: In draft/06-summary.md, paragraph 7, replace "so that all of the jaw carriages advance together by an amount fixed by the geometry of the slots rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw" with "so that all of the jaw carriages advance together through the same inward travel".
28	- **[minor] FIG-1 and FIG-2 disagree on the radial extent of jaw carriage 22 relative to the frame's inner boundary** (figures/FIG-1.md, geometry bullets 5-6; figures/FIG-2.md, geometry bullets 5-6) - Both figures are front views along the pipe axis of the same closed clamp and both label the same parts 22 and 26, but they depict the carriage's inner end at different radii. FIG-1 has the carriage block cross the frame's inner boundary, with the pad lying inboard of that boundary and touching the pipe. FIG-2 has the carriage stop short of the inner circle, so the pad sits at or outboard of the inner boundary. A reader comparing the two views sees jaw carriage 22 and jaw pad 26 occupying inconsistent radial positions in the same frame.
29	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-2.md replace the fifth geometry bullet with: "- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, passing through the inner circle and stopping short of the centre of the drawing area, and reaching the band at its outer end."
30	- **[minor] Claim 13 positively recites a sensor, tool or conduit that no drawing shows, and assigns the mounting boss to a particular frame half** (draft/09-claims.md, claim 13) - Claim 13 recites the sensor, tool or conduit as a positive element of the installed clamp assembly, but no figure shows any sensor, tool or conduit, so a claimed feature is absent from the drawings (37 CFR 1.83(a)). Claim 13 also locates the boss on "the first frame half or the second frame half", whereas the inventor says only that "[t]he frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide"; the description likewise says only "The frame carries a mounting boss 66", and the parallel claims 8 and 17 recite "the frame carries a mounting boss" and "a mounting boss carried by the split pipe clamp". The half-specific wording is both untraced and inconsistent with the other two mounting-boss claims.
31	  - Suggested fix: Replace claim 13 with: "13. The installed clamp assembly of claim 11, wherein the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting one of a sensor, a tool and a conduit."
32	- **[minor] The claimed relationship "outside the annular guide" is not shown in any single view** (figures/FIG-1.md and figures/FIG-2.md; draft/08-detailed-description.md ("The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outsi) - Mounting boss 66 appears only on FIG. 1, which does not show annular guide 36, and annular guide 36 appears only on FIG. 2, which does not show the boss. The relationship recited in claims 8, 13 and 17 and stated in the Detailed Description - the boss lying outside the annular guide - is therefore not depicted anywhere. The fix uses only the relationship the inventor expressly disclosed and adds no new appearance beyond the pad outline already used on FIG. 1.
33	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-2.md: (a) change the front-matter list to "numerals: [22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42, 66]"; (b) add a geometry bullet after the spring bullet: "- A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular pad on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, projecting radially outward and joined to it, lying radially outboard of the channel; shown schematically."; (c) change the sheet line to "Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42, 66."; (d) change the target for 36 to "- 36: the channel outline at the upper left." and add "- 66: well inside the rectangular pad at the upper right."; (e) add "- 66" to the trailing "Numerals shown on this figure" list.
34	- **[minor] FIG-4's stated viewing direction contradicts the arcuate frame band it specifies and the latch orientation of FIG. 1** (figures/FIG-4.md, View line and geometry bullet 1) - The brief says the latch is "seen from the side", but a view from the side of the clamp would show the frame edge as a straight band, not as the arc the same brief calls for; an arcuate frame outline is what a view along the pipe axis produces. FIG. 1 also places the latch at the right-hand break, where the frame runs vertically, while FIG-4 stands the housing on a horizontal frame arc with the wedge pointing down at it. The viewing direction as worded is therefore inconsistent with the geometry specified and with FIG. 1. The geometry itself is sound - the wedge advances radially inward toward the frame and the cam ring within it - so only the view statement needs correcting, and the Brief Description in draft/07-drawings.md ("an enlarged cutaway view of the latch") needs no change.
35	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md replace the first sentence of the View paragraph with: "View: enlarged cutaway view of the latch, seen along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1 and turned so that the frame arc lies across the lower part of the drawing area, with the near wall of the latch housing removed so the parts inside are visible."
36	
37	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
38	the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

tool_use_result.originalFile:
A reusable split pipe clamp is disclosed in which the ring that drives the jaws is itself split, one segment traveling with each half of the frame, and is made into a working ring by the act of closing the frame.

The clamp has a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and joined at a latch end by a releasable latch, so that the frame halves can be swung apart, placed around a pipe, and closed again. Three jaw carriages are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. Each jaw carriage is slidable in a radial guide of the frame and carries a jaw pad that is mounted on the jaw carriage for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface to the pipe. Because each jaw pad pivots, it bears on the pipe without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The cam ring is segmented. A first cam-ring segment is carried by the first frame half and a second cam-ring segment is carried by the second frame half, so each segment stays with its own frame half when the clamp is opened. The first cam-ring segment and the second cam-ring segment have complementary drive faces at the hinge end and complementary drive faces at the latch end. Closing the frame halves brings those complementary drive faces into engagement and couples the cam-ring segments so that they move together as one cam ring about the pipe.

Each jaw carriage carries a follower that is received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The latch carries a wedge. Moving the latch drives the wedge against a ring drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled cam ring through a limited stroke about the pipe. Each oblique slot converts that common rotation into inward travel of its own jaw carriage, so that all of the jaw carriages advance together by an amount fixed by the geometry of the slots rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw. A carriage spring biases each jaw carriage outward, so that releasing the latch retracts the jaw carriages and lifts the jaw pads off the pipe before the frame halves are opened.

The latch has a first position in which it holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second, over-center position in which it drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. The two positions separate the act of capturing the pipe from the act of loading the jaws.

A force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive path between a latch handle of the latch and the wedge. Once all of the jaw pads have contacted the pipe, further movement of the latch handle toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack rather than forcing one jaw pad farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.

An indicator pin is visible on the latch and moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing of the latch when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator reports clamp loading and does not measure pipe diameter.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, a tool or a conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages.

A method of clamping a pipe and a method of releasing the clamp are also disclosed, in which the frame halves are closed about the pipe to couple the cam-ring segments, the latch is moved to the first position and then to the over-center position to rotate the coupled cam ring, and the latch travel that remains after the jaw pads seat is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

- A channel outline drawn as two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, so the band sits within the channel.
- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, none at either division, each drawn as two parallel radial lines between the boundary circles.
- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, passing through the inner circle and stopping short of the centre of the drawing area, and reaching the band at its outer end.
- On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle.
- At the outer end of each carriage a small follower circle lying on the band, and around it a slot drawn as an elongated closed outline through the band, inclined so its long direction is neither purely radial nor purely along the band. The slots share one rotational sense.
- In each slideway a spring drawn as a short zigzag line acting between the carriage and the frame, so that it biases the carriage outward.
- A mounting boss drawn as a small rectangular pad on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, projecting radially outward and lying radially outboard of the channel.

content.content:
(sweep done)
Each jaw carriage carries a follower that is received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The latch carries a wedge. Moving the latch drives the wedge against a ring drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled cam ring through a limited stroke about the pipe. Each oblique slot converts that common rotation into inward travel of its own jaw carriage, so that all of the jaw carriages advance together through the same inward travel. A carriage spring biases each jaw carriage outward, so that releasing the latch retracts the jaw carriages and lifts the jaw pads off the pipe before the frame halves are opened.
13. The installed clamp assembly of claim 11, wherein the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting one of a sensor, a tool and a conduit.

content.text:
All five findings are fixed and the draft is synchronized.

- **Summary ¶7**: the untraced "rather than by separate adjustment of each jaw" contrast is gone; the sentence now says the carriages advance together through the same inward travel.
- **Claim 13**: rewritten as a wherein clause reciting that the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool or conduit, matching claims 8 and 17 and removing both the half-specific location and the positively recited, undrawn sensor/tool/conduit.
- **FIG-2**: the carriage now passes through the inner circle and stops short of the centre, matching FIG-1; the mounting boss is added on the outer boundary at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel, so the "outside the annular guide" relationship is depicted in one view with both 36 and 66 labeled. To hold the sheet at eight numerals, the cam ring label 30 moves off FIG-2 (it is fully identified on FIG-3) and the band remains as unnumbered context; the brief no longer names it.
- **Detailed Description and Brief Description**: the cam ring is no longer said to be shown in FIG. 2 (the annular guide, follower and oblique slot are), the boss sentence now cites FIG. 2, and the FIG. 2 brief description lists the annular guide, the jaw carriages and the mounting boss.
- **FIG-4**: the view is stated as seen along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1, turned so the frame arc lies across the lower part of the drawing area, which agrees with the arcuate band and with the latch orientation of FIG. 1.

Sheet loads are 8/8/8/7 numerals, all four briefs are under the length limit (2765, 2794, 2365, 2791 characters), and all 28 numerals in the table still appear on at least one sheet.

input.summary: Removed the last untraced negative comparative from Summary paragraph 7; rewrote claim 13 so the sensor, tool or conduit is a purpose rather than a positively recited undrawn element and the boss is carried by the frame; made FIG-2's carriage radial extent match FIG-1; added the mounting boss to FIG-2 so the disclosed boss outside the annular guide is depicted in a single view, moving the cam ring label to FIG-3 to keep the sheet at eight numerals; corrected FIG-4's stated viewing direction; and synchronized the Brief Description and Detailed Description figure references.
reasoning: Summary paragraph 7 was the last place asserting a negative comparative the inventor never made. Replacing it with 'advance together through the same inward travel' keeps the disclosed synchronization, which is what claim 6 recites, and drops the contrast with per-jaw adjustment that came from the candidate's own Background rather than from the inventor.

Claim 13 had two problems in one sentence: it made the sensor, tool or conduit a positive element of the assembly although no sheet shows one, and it put the boss on a named frame half although the inventor says only that the frame may carry it. Recasting it as 'the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting one of a sensor, a tool and a conduit' cures both and aligns it with claims 8 and 17, so all three mounting-boss claims now use one form of words.

The coverage failure needed boss 66 and annular guide 36 in one view, but FIG-2 already carried eight numerals and the per-sheet limit is eight. Rather than delete a part or overcrowd the sheet, I moved the cam ring label off FIG-2. The cam ring keeps a dedicated sheet of its own, FIG-3, where it is labeled 30 along with both segments, both pairs of drive faces and the ring drive face, so nothing is lost; on FIG-2 it remains as an unnumbered band that the channel encloses and the slots pass through, which is what that view needs it for.

Because the cam ring is no longer labeled on FIG-2, I moved the two Detailed Description sentences that pointed a reader to FIG. 2 for the cam ring: the annular guide is now the thing shown in FIG. 2 in the retention paragraph, and the follower and oblique slot are the things shown in FIG. 2 in the follower paragraph. The Brief Description of FIG. 2 lists the annular guide, the jaw carriages and the mounting boss for the same reason.

The boss bullet in FIG-2 states only the relationship the inventor disclosed, a pad on the outer boundary lying radially outboard of the channel, and is declared schematic. No new structure, size, or function was added to the specification or claims to support it.

FIG-1 and FIG-2 are the same closed clamp seen the same way, so the carriage had to reach the same radius in both. FIG-2 now has the carriage pass through the inner circle and stop short of the centre, matching FIG-1's carriage that passes the inner boundary and stops short of the pipe, with the pad on its inner end in both.

FIG-4's geometry was right and its view statement was wrong: an arcuate frame band and a wedge advancing radially inward are what a view along the pipe axis gives, not a side view. I corrected only the view sentence, so the drive path the disclosure describes is unchanged and the Brief Description needed no edit.

Both FIG-2 and FIG-4 went over the length limit after these insertions. I trimmed only invented rendering constraints, a duplicated schematic declaration, a stroke-count phrase for the slideways, and page-placement words for the housing, and folded the rod's mounting into the single closing declaration, leaving every disclosed body, contact, opening and relationship in place.

FIG-4 is now stated as seen along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1, consistent with its arcuate frame band and with the latch position in FIG. 1. In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2.
