Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

All six findings are fixed.

- **FIG-4 latch linkage**: the handle pivot on the side wall, the two-armed lever, the inner arm resting on the stack, and the stack end plates are gone. The handle is now a straight lever extending outward and downward from the housing with its inner end reaching the top of the stack so the stack lies between the handle and the wedge, which is the only drive-path relationship the disclosure gives.
- **FIG-4 wedge**: the wedge now extends out of the housing to the arcuate band so its inclined lower face meets the band; the non-contact gap assertion is removed, matching the description and claims 1, 11 and 14.
- **FIG-4 indicator rod**: it stands on the upper end of the stack, offset to the left of the housing centre, and passes through the top wall so its projecting end is visible; the handle's inner end reaches the stack from the right, so the two no longer occupy the same space, and the rod moves with the stack.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Ledger scope: the sole inventor authority is input/disclosure.md, reproduced verbatim as the single USER turn in input/conversation.md; input/brief.md was used only for formalities (title, applicant/inventor, no priority claim, no federal sponsorship). No prior-art search was run per input/brief.md, so the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete; Background prior-art characterizations were not required to trace to the inventor and are left to the later citation review. Rendered images were not inspected.

5	Clean traces (representative): "first semicircular frame half"/"second semicircular frame half", "hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end" -> draft/08 para 5 and claims 1, 11, 14; "Three radial jaw carriages ... Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter" -> draft/06 para 3, draft/08 paras 13-15, claims 1, 10; "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half" -> draft/08 paras 21, 25, claims 1, 7, 11, 14; "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring" -> draft/08 para 27 and claims 1, 7, 11, 14, with numerals 44/46/48/50 now carrying distinct first/second names in both draft/08 and draft/numerals.md; "follower received in a respective oblique slot" and "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" -> draft/08 para 31 and claims 1, 6, 14; "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke" -> draft/08 para 35, claims 1, 11, 14; "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released" -> draft/08 para 17, claims 1, 9, 16; the two latch positions -> draft/08 para 37, claim 5; "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge" -> draft/08 paras 39, 41, claims 1-3, 11, 14; "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range ... does not measure pipe diameter" -> draft/08 para 43, claims 4, 12, 15; the install and remove sequences -> draft/08 paras 47, 49, claims 14, 16; "mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit ... does not participate in jaw synchronization" -> draft/08 paras 9, 23, claims 8, 13, 17. All 28 numerals in draft/numerals.md are used in draft/08, each with a single consistent meaning, and the four figure numeral sets union exactly to the table with no orphans or extras. Sections 02 and 03 correctly read "Not applicable". No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, unresolved alternatives, or internal comments remain in draft/ or figures/, and no application text uses "by way of example", "any closed outline", or similar renderer-justifying breadth - the schematic conventions stay confined to the figure briefs. There are no sectional views, so no section-line designation consistency question arises. Figure-to-figure orientation is consistent (hinge/left, latch/right in FIGS. 1-3; first frame half 12 and first cam-ring segment 32 both the upper member; 44/46 at the left junction and 48/50 at the right).
6	
7	Judgment calls I did not flag, with reasons: the roughly equal angular spacing of the three carriages/slideways/slots and their placement clear of the frame breaks (entailed by "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame" plus "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages", and consistent across FIGS. 1-3); the common rotational sense of the oblique slots (entailed by one rotation producing inward travel at all three); the follower drawn at the outer end of each carriage and the cam-ring band set toward the outer boundary inside its channel (forced by "retained in an annular guide" plus the boss lying "outside the annular guide"); the short plain ring drive face in FIG. 3 being "clear of the junctions and of the three slots" (a non-overlap statement only - the brief fixes no circumferential end position, taper, angle or depth for that functional face, and the part itself is affirmatively disclosed); claim 6's "same inward travel at every jaw carriage" ("synchronized ... rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others"); and the FIG. 1 page-scale statement about the pipe occupying roughly the middle third of the drawing width (non-substantive placement).
8	
9	Four defects require correction before render. Two are critical and both sit in figures/FIG-4.md. First, the brief now states that the wedge "extend[s] downward out of the housing to the arcuate band so that its inclined lower face meets the band", where the band is expressly "representing frame structure". That is an affirmative contact-topology assertion putting the wedge in bearing contact with the frame, whereas the inventor discloses only that the wedge bears on a drive face of the cam ring; it also contradicts draft/08 line 35 and claims 1, 11 and 14, and FIG. 4 depicts neither cam ring 30 nor ring drive face 54. Second, the brief mounts the indicator rod by "standing on the upper end of the stack of springs" - a drive coupling and contact joint that no inventor passage describes; the disclosure correlates pin movement with stack compression but never says what carries the pin. A prior reviewer's suggested wording is not inventor support, so both statements must come out. Two smaller items: figures/FIG-2.md draws the annular frame body as continuous concentric circles while dividing only the cam-ring band at the left and right, which contradicts FIG. 1 and draft/08 (a split frame whose halves each carry a segment); and draft/07-drawings.md describes FIG. 2 as revealing only "the annular guide, the jaw carriages and the mounting boss" although that figure also carries numerals 26, 38, 40 and 42 that draft/08 says are shown there. Each finding below carries a drop-in fix.

12	
13	- **Source fidelity is clean before rendering** (fail): Ledger scope: the sole inventor authority is input/disclosure.md, reproduced verbatim as the single USER turn in input/conversation.md; input/brief.md was used only for formalities (title, applicant/inventor, no priority claim, no federal sponsorship). Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter" -> draft/06 para 3, draft/08 paras 13-15, claims 1, 10; "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half" -> draft/08 paras 21, 25, claims 1, 7, 11, 14; "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring" -> draft/08 para 27 and claims 1, 7, 11, 14, with numerals 44/46/48/50 now carrying distinct first/second names in both draft/08 and draft/numerals.md; "follower received in a respective oblique slot" and "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" -> draft/08 para 31 and claims 1, 6, 14; "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke" -> draft/08 para 35, claims 1, 11, 14; "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released" -> draft/08 para 17, claims 1, 9, 16; the two latch positions -> draft/08 para 37, claim 5; "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge" -> draft/08 paras 39, 41, claims 1-3, 
16	  - FIG. 4 brief puts the wedge in bearing contact with frame structure, not with the disclosed ring drive face
17	  - FIG. 4 brief mounts the indicator pin on the top of the spring stack, a coupling the inventor never disclosed
18	  - FIG. 2 brief draws the frame as one continuous annular body while dividing only the cam-ring band, contradicting FIG. 1 and the description
19	  - Brief Description of FIG. 2 omits parts that FIG. 2 alone is said to show
20	
21	## Reviewer findings
22	
23	- **[critical] FIG. 4 brief puts the wedge in bearing contact with frame structure, not with the disclosed ring drive face** (figures/FIG-4.md, "Geometry to draw" bullets 1 and 4; conflicts with draft/08-detailed-description.md line 35 and claims) - The brief defines the arcuate band as "representing frame structure" and then states that the wedge's "inclined lower face meets the band". Contact topology of a functional inclined face is substantive even where the brief calls the parts schematic. The inventor discloses only one thing the wedge bears on: "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." There is no affirmative passage anywhere in input/disclosure.md or the single USER turn of input/conversation.md stating that the wedge contacts, bears on, or lands on the frame; the nearest passage is the one quoted, which names the cam ring's drive face as the driven surface. As briefed, FIG. 4 shows neither cam ring 30 nor ring drive face 54, so the only engagement it depicts is the unsupported wedge-to-frame contact, which also contradicts the description ("Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30") and claim 1 ("a wedge ... positioned to bear on a ring drive face of the cam ring").
24	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md: (a) insert a new bullet immediately after the arcuate-band bullet reading "- Drawn within the arcuate band and following it, a narrower arcuate strip representing the cam ring held in the annular guide of the frame, and on its outward side a short plain drive face facing the wedge; the strip and the drive face are shown schematically."; (b) replace the wedge bullet with "- Below the stack of springs a wedge drawn as a block whose lower end is an inclined straight face, the wedge extending downward out of the housing to the narrower arcuate strip so that its inclined lower face meets the short plain drive face of that strip."; (c) change the front-matter line to "numerals: [18, 30, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64]", change the sheet line to "Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 18, 30, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64.", add "- 30" and "- 54" to the "## Numerals shown on this figure" list, and add the placement targets "- 30: the narrower arcuate strip, to the left of the wedge." and "- 54: the short plain drive face where the inclined lower face of the wedge meets the strip." In draft/07-drawings.md replace the FIG. 4 sentence with "FIG. 4 is an enlarged cutaway view of the latch, showing the latch handle, the force-limiting spring stack, the indicator pin, the wedge and the ring drive face of the cam ring on which the wedge bears." In draft/08-detailed-description.md line 35 change "shown in FIG. 3, and rotates" to "shown in FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and rotates".

Standing on a part is a contact joint and, here, a drive coupling that makes the pin a follower of stack compression - substantive structure, not an outline choice, and it remains substantive even though the brief says "the rod with its mounting ... shown schematically". The inventor discloses the pin's visibility and its motion relative to a housing edge at a compression range, but never what carries or drives the pin; it could equally be driven by the wedge, the handle, or an intermediate lever. No affirmative USER passage describes the pin's mounting. The description and claims are correspondingly silent (draft/08 line 43: "An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 ..."), so the brief verbalizes structure the application does not carry. 5	A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. 12

# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

5:Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.
7:Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.
13:Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.
21:A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.
23:The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2.
25:The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.
31:Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.
35:The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.
39:Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

I fixed them by deletion rather than by adding text to draft/08 to support them: the wedge now ends clear of the frame band instead of bearing on it, and the indicator rod terminates inside the housing clear of the spring stack instead of standing on it. Adding a wedge-to-frame contact or a pin-to-stack connection to the specification would have manufactured an undisclosed kinematic relationship, and in the pin's case would have made the indicator track handle travel rather than stack compression, which is the opposite of what the disclosure says the indicator reports.

Removing the pin's driving connection from the drawing loses nothing the claims need. The claims recite that the indicator pin moves relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range; the sheet only has to show a visible pin projecting through the housing wall past that fixed edge, which it now does. How the pin is driven was never disclosed and is therefore not claimed.

For FIG. 3, 'clear of the junctions' was a circumferential position for a functional drive face with no source basis, and it fought the rest of the disclosure: the wedge is carried by the latch, and the latch sits at the right break, which is a junction. Deleting it keeps the sheet neutral about where on the ring the face lies while retaining the slot clearance, which is only legibility.

The FIG. 4 frame break is an affirmative disclosed fact, that the halves are releasably joined at the latch end, so adding it to the enlarged view corrects a contradiction with FIG. 1 rather than inventing geometry. Numeral 52's target was broadened to the interior of the wedge block once the inclined face reference was removed, consistent with preferring a broad interior target.

No affirmative USER passage describes where the indicator pin's lower end sits or whether it touches, is separated from, or is driven by the spring stack. The only disclosed relationship is functional and points the other way: the pin moves in response to the stack's compression state. Asserting a gap is therefore untraced substance and is at odds with the disclosed function. The nearest source passage is the whole of the inventor's statement about the pin, which says nothing about the pin's lower end: "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range."
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, delete the untraced clause so the bullet reads: "A slender vertical rod, offset to the left of the housing centre, its lower end terminating within the housing, rising within the housing and passing through the top wall so that its upper end projects beyond the top wall and is visible outside the housing."
- **[major] FIG-3 verbalizes contact topology of the functional cam-ring drive faces ("meet across the width of the band")** (figures/FIG-3.md, geometry bullet 2 ("...two short faces of matching outline that meet across the width of the band, so ) - The hinge-end and latch-end drive faces are functional drive surfaces. The source discloses only that they are complementary and that closing the halves couples the segments; it does not disclose that the faces abut over the full radial width of the ring, nor any other contact topology, taper, angle, or radial end position. Under the functional-surface rule, a statement that the faces "meet across the width of the band" is substantive even though the brief adds "The shape of these end faces is shown schematically". A minimally specific generic abutment may remain; the width-spanning contact statement may not.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, revise the bullet to: "The band is divided into an upper arcuate segment and a lower arcuate segment by two junctions, one at the left and one at the right. At each junction the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment are two short faces of matching outline that abut one another, so the two segments read as separate solids in contact. The shape of these end faces is shown schematically."
- **[minor] FIG-1 draws the jaw pad unconnected to the jaw carriage, contrary to the source and to FIG-2** (figures/FIG-1.md, geometry bullet 6 ("Between the inner end of each carriage block and the pipe circle, a small block wh) - The source states that each carriage "carries" the pivoting jaw pad, and FIG-2 correctly shows the pad "joined to the carriage at a small circle". FIG-1 instead places the pad merely "between" the carriage and the pipe with no stated attachment, which would render an unsupported floating part and conflicts with FIG-2 and with the description ("Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement").
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, revise the bullet to: "On the inner end of each carriage block, a small block whose inner edge is a concave arc meeting the pipe circle, so that this small block, and not the carriage block, contacts the pipe."
- **[minor] FIG-4 handle direction is inconsistent with the view rotation stated in the same brief** (figures/FIG-4.md, view line and geometry bullet 6 (handle "extending outward and downward to the right")) - FIG-4 states the latch is seen "along the pipe axis as in FIG. 1 and turned so that the frame arc lies across the lower part of the drawing area", with the housing standing on that band. Under that rotation the outward direction is upward, so FIG-1's handle direction (radially outward and downward to the right, with the frame at the left) maps to upward and to the right. Retaining the FIG-1 wording verbatim in FIG-4 makes the lever run downward into the arcuate frame band that the same brief places across the lower part of the sheet and extends "to the left and to the right".
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, revise the handle bullet to: "A handle drawn as a straight lever extending upward and to the right from the housing, away from the arcuate band and ending clear of the housing, its inner end reaching into the housing to the top of the stack of springs so that the stack lies between the handle and the wedge."
- **[minor] Cam ring 30 is said to be shown in FIG. 2 but is not among FIG-2's numerals** (draft/07-drawings.md FIG. 2 sentence; draft/08-detailed-description.md para. beginning "A cam ring 30 is retained..."; f) - The Brief Description says FIG. 2 reveals "the cam ring", and the detailed description says "The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate...". The FIG-2 brief does draw the cam ring (the "narrow band of two concentric arcs") but omits numeral 30 from both its front-matter numeral list and its placement targets, so the part the text says is revealed in that view carries no designation there. Every other part named in the FIG. 2 sentence of the Brief Description (annular guide 36, oblique slots 38, followers 40, jaw carriages 22, jaw pads 26, carriage springs 42, mounting boss 66) is labeled.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, add 30 to the front-matter numeral list and to the "## Numerals shown on this figure" list, and add the placement target: "- 30: the narrow band at the upper right, clear of the slot outlines, identifying the cam ring."
- **[minor] FIG-4 schematic list refers to a "mounting" for the rod that is not in the geometry** (figures/FIG-4.md, final line ("The housing, the stack of springs, the wedge, the rod with its mounting, and the handle a) - The geometry list describes only the slender vertical rod passing through the top wall; no mounting, bracket, or guide for the rod is specified anywhere in the brief, in numerals.md, or in the description. The phrase "with its mounting" therefore designates an undefined element and reads as a dangling drafting remnant that a renderer could resolve as an invented structure.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, change the final line to: "The housing, the stack of springs, the wedge, the rod and the handle are shown schematically."

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, as shown in FIG. 2.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

# FIG-2

---
figure: FIG. 2
numerals: [22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42]
---


View: front interior view of the closed clamp along the pipe axis. Patent line drawing, black on white, no shading or color. Near side frame material is omitted to reveal the interior, a depiction convention. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

Geometry to draw:

- An annular body drawn as concentric outer and inner boundary circles centered in the drawing area, the space between them open and the region inside the inner circle empty. No pipe is drawn.
- Within that space, a narrow band of two concentric arcs set toward the outer boundary, divided at the left and at the right.
- A channel outline drawn as two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, so the band sits within the channel.
- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, none at either division, each drawn as two parallel radial lines between the boundary circles.
- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, passing through the inner circle and stopping short of the centre of the drawing area, and reaching the band at its outer end.
- On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle.
- At the outer end of each carriage a small follower circle lying on the band, and around it a slot drawn as an elongated closed outline through the band, inclined so its long direction is neither purely radial nor purely along the band. The slots share one rotational sense.
- In each slideway a spring drawn as a short zigzag line acting between the carriage and the frame, so that it biases the carriage outward.
- A small rectangular projection on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, standing radially outward and lying radially outboard of the channel.

The band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically.

Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42.

content.text:
All six findings are fixed and the sheets, briefs, numeral table and text are back in step.

- **FIG-4**: the indicator rod bullet no longer states any relationship to the spring stack (its lower end simply terminates within the housing); the handle now extends upward and to the right, away from the arcuate band, matching the stated view rotation; the dangling "with its mounting" phrase is gone from the schematic list.
- **FIG-3**: the segment end faces now "abut one another" rather than meeting across the width of the band, so no contact topology is asserted for the functional drive faces.
- **FIG-1**: the concave-edged pad now sits on the inner end of each carriage block, matching "each jaw carriage carries a jaw pad" and FIG-2's pivot joint.
- **FIG-2**: numeral 30 is added for the cam ring. Because eight numerals per sheet is the ceiling, numeral 66 moved to FIG. 1, which already labels the mounting boss; FIG-2 still draws that structure as an unnumbered generic projection radially outboard of the channel, so the disclosed relationship stays visible. No part, numeral definition or specification text was deleted.
- **draft/07**: FIG. 1 now recites the hinge, latch, jaw carriages and mounting boss; FIG. 2 recites the annular guide, cam ring, oblique slots and followers, jaw carriages, jaw pads and carriage springs.
- **draft/08**: the single figure citation for the mounting boss now points to FIG. 1, where it is labeled; the sentence's substance (boss outside the annular guide 36) is unchanged.

All four briefs are within the 2800 character limit, every sheet lists at most eight numerals, and all 28 numerals in the table appear on at least one sheet. Claims, summary, abstract and numerals.md are untouched.

input.summary: Fixed all six findings. FIG-4 drops the untraced pin-to-stack spatial statement, corrects the handle direction to match its own view rotation, and removes the dangling rod "mounting". FIG-3 replaces the width-spanning abutment of the cam-ring drive faces with a generic abutment. FIG-1 joins the jaw pad to the inner end of the carriage. Cam ring 30 is now labeled on FIG. 2, with mounting boss 66 relabeled on FIG. 1 to stay within eight numerals per sheet, and the Brief Description and the one affected figure citation in the detailed description are synchronized.
reasoning: The two major findings were both figure-only assertions about functional parts, so both were fixed by deletion rather than by adding support to the text. The rod bullet now says only that its lower end terminates within the housing, which leaves the disclosed function (the pin moves relative to the fixed edge when the stack enters a predetermined compression range) untouched and asserts neither contact nor a gap. The cam-ring end faces now simply abut, which keeps the two segments reading as separate solids in contact without claiming they meet over the full radial width.

FIG-4's handle was rotated to run upward and to the right. FIG-1 shows the lever extending radially outward from the frame; FIG-4 is the same view turned so the frame arc lies across the lower part of the sheet, which maps radially outward to upward. Keeping FIG-1's literal wording would have driven the lever into the frame band. Only the drawing direction changed, not the disclosed relationship that the handle acts through the stack onto the wedge.

The cam-ring labeling finding could not be satisfied by simply adding numeral 30 to FIG-2, because that sheet already carried the maximum of eight numerals. Rather than delete a part or its supporting text, I redistributed: 30 goes on FIG. 2, where the cam ring is drawn as the band that the slots and followers work in, and 66 is labeled on FIG. 1, which already showed and numbered the mounting boss. FIG-2 still draws the boss structure, as an unnumbered generic projection radially outboard of the channel, so the disclosed relationship that the boss lies outside the annular guide remains visible in the view that shows the guide.

That redistribution required two conforming text edits and no substantive ones: the FIG. 1 sentence in the Brief Description now recites the parts labeled there including the mounting boss, the FIG. 2 sentence drops the boss and keeps the cam ring, and the detailed description sentence about the boss now cites FIG. 1 instead of FIG. 2 while keeping its content, that the mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, word for word.

FIG-1's pad is now carried on the inner end of the carriage block rather than floating between the carriage and the pipe, which conforms the sheet to the description that each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 mounted on it, and to FIG-2's pivot joint. While trimming FIG-2 back under the character limit I also made numeral 26's target read as the concave edged pad rather than the ambiguous 'pad block', since the sheet now shows two rectangular pads.

figures/FIG-4.md: handle bullet now extends upward and to the right from the housing, away from the arcuate band, consistent with the stated view rotation.
figures/FIG-4.md: closing schematic sentence now reads 'The housing, the stack of springs, the wedge, the rod and the handle are shown schematically.', removing the undefined rod mounting.
figures/FIG-3.md: the two end faces at each junction now 'abut one another' instead of meeting across the width of the band.
figures/FIG-1.md: the concave edged block is now placed on the inner end of each carriage block rather than merely between the carriage and the pipe.
figures/FIG-2.md: numeral 30 added to the front matter list, the placement targets and the numerals list, targeted at the narrow band at the upper right.

figures/FIG-2.md: numeral 66 removed from the front matter list, the placement targets and the numerals list; the structure remains drawn as an unnumbered small rectangular projection standing radially outward from the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel, and the canonical part name is no longer used on this sheet.
figures/FIG-2.md: numeral 26 target changed to the concave edged pad at the lower right; minor wording trims to the annular body and band bullets to stay within the character limit.

draft/07-drawings.md: FIG. 1 sentence now recites the hinge, the releasable latch, the jaw carriages and the mounting boss; FIG. 2 sentence now recites the annular guide, the cam ring, the oblique slots and followers, the jaw carriages, the jaw pads and the carriage springs.

input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged this turn; no claim, Background citation, or substantive Detailed Description passage was edited. The distinguishing combination stands as drafted: frame closure couples two separately retained cam-ring segments through complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces so they move as one ring, latch travel drives a wedge against a ring drive face to rotate the coupled ring through a limited stroke, oblique slots convert that rotation into the same inward travel at every jaw carriage, and a force-limiting spring stack in the drive path between latch handle and wedge takes up the remaining over-center travel after all pads contact while an indicator pin reports load rather than diameter. Each figure correction was made in the direction that protects that recital rather than qualifying it: FIG-3 no longer over-specifies the coupling faces the independent claims depend on, and FIG-4 no longer implies a mechanical path between the indicator pin and the spring stack that the claims do not recite and the disclosure does not describe.
input.answer:
All six findings are resolved and the figures, briefs, numeral table and text are synchronized.

FIG-4: the indicator rod bullet now states only that the rod is offset to the left of the housing centre, that its lower end terminates within the housing, and that it rises through the top wall so its upper end projects and is visible outside; no contact or clearance relative to the force-limiting spring stack is asserted. The handle extends upward and to the right from the housing, away from the arcuate band, which is what FIG-1's radially outward direction becomes under the rotation this brief states, and its inner end still reaches the top of the stack so the stack lies between handle and wedge. The closing line now reads that the housing, the stack of springs, the wedge, the rod and the handle are shown schematically, with no reference to a rod mounting.

FIG-3: at each junction the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment are two short faces of matching outline that abut one another, so the segments read as separate solids in contact without any statement about how far across the band they meet.

FIG-1: the concave edged block now sits on the inner end of each carriage block and meets the pipe circle, matching the description that each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 mounted on it for pivoting movement, and matching the pivot joint in FIG-2.

FIG-2 and the drawing descriptions: numeral 30 now labels the cam ring on the sheet that draws it as the band carrying the oblique slots and followers. Because that sheet was already at the eight numeral ceiling, numeral 66 is now carried by FIG. 1, which already showed the mounting boss. FIG-2 still draws that structure as an unnumbered small rectangular projection standing radially outward from the outer boundary circle at the upper right and lying radially outboard of the channel, so the disclosed relationship remains visible in the view that shows the annular guide. The FIG. 1 sentence of the Brief Description now recites the hinge, the releasable latch, the jaw carriages and the mounting boss; the FIG. 2 sentence recites the annular guide, the cam ring, the oblique slots and followers, the jaw carriages, the jaw pads and the carriage springs. In the detailed description, the mounting boss sentence keeps its content and now cites FIG. 1.

Claims, summary, abstract, field, background and numerals.md are unchanged. Every sheet lists at most eight numerals, each of the 28 numerals in the table appears on at least one sheet and is used in the description, and all four briefs are within the 2800 character limit.
